Rashi on Shabbat 116a:10:1.hebrew: דבי אבידן - ספרים שכתבו להם המינין להתווכח עם ישראל, ומקום שמתווכחים שם קרי ליה בי אבידן:
Rashi on Shabbat 116a:10:1.english: Of the house of Abidan - Books that the heretics wrote for themselves to debate with Israel, and the place where they debate is called the house of Abidan.

Rashi on Shabbat 116a:10:2.hebrew: אין ולא - זימנין אמר ליה אין, זימנין א"ל לא:
Rashi on Shabbat 116a:10:2.english: Yes and no - Sometimes he said to him yes, [and] sometimes he said to him no.

Rashi on Shabbat 116a:10:3.hebrew: לבי נצרפי - ע"ז, וכך שמה:
Rashi on Shabbat 116a:10:3.english: To the house of Nitzrefei - [This is] idolatry, and such is its name.

Rashi on Shabbat 116a:10:4.hebrew: וקשה לי - ששורשן נעשו גבשושית, ולדחותם בקש בא:
Rashi on Shabbat 116a:10:4.english: And [it is] difficult for me - For its roots have become a mound, and he came to put them off with a straw [i.e., a flimsy excuse].

Rashi on Shabbat 116a:10:5.hebrew: אמרי ליה ניעקריה קשה לי דוכתיה - שתהא שם גומא, אי נמי: נסיתיו וקשה לי ריחו. וכל זה שהיו מתייראין רב ורבא מלכת לבי אבידן, שמא מתוך שיתווכחו יעמדו עליהם ויהרגום:
Rashi on Shabbat 116a:10:5.english: They said to him, "We will uproot it"; [he replied,] "Its place is difficult for me" - [Meaning] that there will be a pit there; alternatively, [he meant,] "I have tried it, and its odor is unpleasant to me." And all of this [was] because Rav and Rava were afraid to go to the house of Abidan, lest as a result of their debating, [the gentiles] would rise up against them and kill them.

Rashi on Shabbat 116a:10:6.english: I am [one] of them - They are my acquaintances.

Rashi on Shabbat 116a:1:1.hebrew: שאין זה מקומה - שאינה ראויה לכאן, דלאו בהליכות מסעות משתעי לעיל מינה, אלא בדגלים היתה ראויה ליכתב בפרשת במדבר סיני:
Rashi on Shabbat 116a:1:1.english: That this is not its place - For it is not fitting [to be] here, since [Scripture] above it is not speaking of the marches of the journeys; rather, it was fitting to be written with [the section of] the banners in the portion of Bemidbar Sinai.

Rashi on Shabbat 116a:1:2.hebrew: לא מן השם הוא זה - לא זה השם של טעמי הסימניות, דמקומה הוא, דפרשה זו בתחלת מסע שנסעו מהר סיני איירי, כדכתיב לעיל מיניה: ויהי בחדש השני בשנה השנית בעשרים לחדש נעלה הענן וגו':
Rashi on Shabbat 116a:1:2.english: It is not for that reason - This is not the reason for the signs, for it is [indeed] its [proper] place, since this section deals with the beginning of the journey when they journeyed from Mount Sinai, as it is written above it: "And it came to pass in the second month, in the second year, on the twentieth [day] of the month, the cloud was lifted, etc."

Rashi on Shabbat 116a:2:1.hebrew: ז' ספרי תורה - דפרשה זו ספר לעצמו, נמצא שלמעלה ספר לעצמו [ושלמטה ספר לעצמו], הואיל וזה מקומה. נמצא ספר וידבר נחלק לג' ספרים:
Rashi on Shabbat 116a:2:1.english: Seven books of the Torah - For this section is a book unto itself; thus, what is above [it] is a book unto itself [and what is below it is a book unto itself], since this is its place. Thus, the Book of Vayedaber [Numbers] is divided into three books.

Rashi on Shabbat 116a:3:1.hebrew: עתידה פרשה זו - לעתיד שיהו כל הפורעניות בטלין, ולא ידאגו לפורענות, ויצר הרע בטל:
Rashi on Shabbat 116a:3:1.english: This portion will in the future - [That is,] in the future, when all calamities will cease, and they will not worry about calamity, and the evil inclination [will be] abolished.

Rashi on Shabbat 116a:3:2.hebrew: מאחרי ה' - בתוך ג' ימים למסעם, התאוו האספסוף תאוה להתרעם על הבשר, כדי למרוד בהקב"ה:
Rashi on Shabbat 116a:3:2.english: From after God - Within three days of their journey, the rabble felt a craving to complain about meat, in order to rebel against the Holy One, Blessed be He.

Rashi on Shabbat 116a:4:1.hebrew: הגליונין - קלפים חלקים. וקס"ד השתא דבכל צדדין שיהו חלקים קמיבעיא ליה, כגון חלק שלמעלה ושלמטה, ושנמחק כתבו ונעשה חלק:
Rashi on Shabbat 116a:4:1.english: The blank folios - Blank parchments. And [the Gemara] presently assumes that it is asking about all ways in which they may be blank, such as the blank [margin] above and below, and [parchment] whose writing was erased and became blank.

Rashi on Shabbat 116a:4:2.hebrew: בלה שאני - דכיון שבלה, אף הגליון בטל. וכי מיבעיא ליה, שהגליונין קיימים אלא שהכתב הלך:
Rashi on Shabbat 116a:4:2.english: Worn is different - For since it is worn, the blank folio is also nullified. And when [the dilemma] is raised, [it is a case] where the blank folios are intact, except that the writing is gone.

Rashi on Shabbat 116a:5:1.english: And let it be derived due to its blank parchment - That is, the entire Torah scroll.

Rashi on Shabbat 116a:5:2.english: The place of the writing - [meaning,] that which was erased.

Rashi on Shabbat 116a:5:3.hebrew: לא מבעיא לי - דודאי מיגרע גרע, דכי קדיש מעיקרא לאו לשם גליון חלק קדיש אלא אדעתא דכתב, וכיון דאזל ליה כתב, פקע מקדושתיה:
Rashi on Shabbat 116a:5:3.english: It is not a dilemma for me - For it is certainly inferior, since when it was originally sanctified, it was not sanctified as a blank margin, but rather on account of the writing; and once the writing is gone, its sanctity ceases.

Rashi on Shabbat 116a:5:4.hebrew: של מעלה ומטה - דמתחלה לשם חלק קדיש, והשתא כשנמחק כתב הספר נמי חלק הוא:
Rashi on Shabbat 116a:5:4.english: [The blank space] above and below - For from the outset it was sanctified to be blank, and now too, when the writing of the scroll has been erased, it is blank.

Rashi on Shabbat 116a:5:5.hebrew: שבתחלת הספר ושבסוף הספר - שכולן היו כתובין כמגילה כס"ת, ואמרי' בב"ב בפ"ק (דף יג:): ראשו כדי לגול עמוד, סופו כדי לגול היקף — להקיף כל הכרך:
Rashi on Shabbat 116a:5:5.english: That [are] at the beginning of the scroll and that [are] at the end of the scroll - For all of them were written as a scroll, like a Torah scroll, and we say in Bava Batra in the first chapter (13b): "Its beginning [must have enough blank parchment] to roll around a roller, [and] its end [must have enough] to roll around the circumference" — to wrap around the entire scroll.

Rashi on Shabbat 116a:5:6.hebrew: ה"ג ותיפוק ליה משום ההוא דגייז ושדי - והכי פירושא: ותיפוק לי', דאע"ג דאין בו כדי ללקט פ"ה אותיות, הוה ליה למיתני בברייתא מצילין משום ההוא ריוח של מעלה ומטה, אלא לאו פשוט מיניה דאין מצילין? ומשני: דגייז ושדי — שנחתכו הגליונים ולא נשתייר בו אלא מקום הכתב:
Rashi on Shabbat 116a:5:6.english: This is how we read [the text]: And derive it due to that [blank area]; where it was cut and thrown - And this is its explanation: Let it be derived — even though there is not enough in it to compile eighty-five letters, [the Tanna] should have taught in the baraita "one rescues [it]" due to that space above and below; rather, is it not resolved from this that one does not rescue [them]? And [the Gemara] answers: "Where it was cut and thrown" — [meaning] that the blank margins were cut off and nothing remained of it except the place of the writing.

Rashi on Shabbat 116a:6:1.hebrew: מטמא את הידים - אם נגע בו ונגע בתרומה, פוסלה, דמגזירת י"ח דבר היא (לעיל שבת דף יד.):
Rashi on Shabbat 116a:6:1.english: Renders the hands ritually impure - If one touched it and [then] touched terumah, he disqualifies it, for it is from the decree of the eighteen enactments (above, Shabbat 14a).

Rashi on Shabbat 116a:6:2.hebrew: דילמא אגב ס"ת - שלא נמחק כתב הספר, אלא כולו קיים, וזה נגע בגליונים. וכי מבעיא לן — בנמחק הספר, ואין כאן קדושה אלא משום גליון ששמשו בעודו קיים:
Rashi on Shabbat 116a:6:2.english: Perhaps [when it is] part of a Torah scroll - [That is,] where the writing of the scroll was not erased, rather the entire [scroll] is intact and this [person] touched the blank margins. Whereas when we raised our question, [it was] where the scroll was erased, and there is no sanctity here except on account of [its being] a blank margin that served it while it was intact.

Rashi on Shabbat 116a:7:1.hebrew: ספרי מינין - משרתים לע"ז, וכתבו להן תורה, נביאים, כתובים, כתב אשורית ולשון הקודש:
Rashi on Shabbat 116a:7:1.english: Scrolls of heretics - [People who] serve idolatry, and wrote for themselves Torah, Prophets, [and] Writings [in] Assyrian script and the Holy Tongue.

Rashi on Shabbat 116a:7:2.english: And the scrolls of the heretics themselves, does one rescue [them]? - [This is said] as a rhetorical question.

Rashi on Shabbat 116a:7:3.english: The scrolls of heretics are like blank folios - Like blank parchments upon which [nothing] was ever written.

Rashi on Shabbat 116a:8:1.english: Cuts out - [He] cuts the pieces of the parchment [at] the place of the Name.

Rashi on Shabbat 116a:8:2.hebrew: שאפי' רודף אדם להורגו - על עצמו קאמר:
Rashi on Shabbat 116a:8:2.english: For even [if] a person pursues [him] to kill him - He is speaking about himself.

Rashi on Shabbat 116a:8:3.hebrew: שהללו - נכרים העובדים ע"ז אינן מכירין, שהרי בכך גדלו וכך למדום אבותם:
Rashi on Shabbat 116a:8:3.english: For these - gentiles who worship idolatry do not recognize [God], for they grew up with this and thus their fathers taught them.

Rashi on Shabbat 116a:8:4.hebrew: ואחר הדלת והמזוזה שמת זכרונך - זכרון הוא בידך, ואינה שכחה לך, אלא שהשלכת אותי אחרי הדלת:
Rashi on Shabbat 116a:8:4.english: And behind the door and the doorpost you placed your memory - It is a remembrance in your hand, and it is not forgotten by you; rather, you have cast Me behind the door.

Rashi on Shabbat 116a:9:1.hebrew: כך אין מצילין אותן - אפי' בחול:
Rashi on Shabbat 116a:9:1.english: So too, they are not rescued - Even on a weekday.

Tosafot on Shabbat 116a:11:1.hebrew: פילוסופא - מין, כדפי' בקונטרס. ורבינו שמע [מיהודי אחד שבא מארץ יון ואמר] דבלשון יון "פלוספוס" הוא דוד החכמה. ואית דגרסי "פילא סבא", והוא לשון לצון, שחוק; כדאמר באיכה רבתי: "דפלי ביהודאי" — פירוש: ששחק ונתלוצץ:
Tosafot on Shabbat 116a:11:1.english: Pilosofa - [This means] a heretic, as [Rashi] explained in the Kuntres. And our Rabbi heard from a certain Jew who came from the land of Greece, who said that in the Greek language "filosofos" means "lover of wisdom." And there are those who read "pila sava," and it is an expression of mockery [and] laughter; as it says in Eikhah Rabbati: "defalei biYehudai" — meaning: that he laughed and mocked.

Tosafot on Shabbat 116a:3:1.hebrew: פורענות ראשונה ויסעו וא"ר חנינא שסרו מאחרי השם - פי' בקונטרס שמאז התחילו לשאול בשר. ואומר ר"י דאין נ"ל כן, אלא פורענות ראשונה כדאמר במדרש (ילמדנו): "ויסעו" — שנסעו מהר סיני דרך שלשת ימים, כתינוק היוצא מבית הספר שבורח לו והולך לו, כך היו בורחים מהר סיני דרך שלשת ימים, לפי שלמדו הרבה תורה בסיני. אמר הקב"ה: נסמוך פורענות לפורענות? לאו! אלא נפסוק פרשת "ויהי בנסוע הארון":
Tosafot on Shabbat 116a:3:1.english: The first punishment [is]: "And they traveled..." and Rabbi Ḥanina said that they turned from after God - Rashi explained that from then on they began to ask for meat. And Rabbeinu Yitzchak says that this does not appear [correct] to me; rather, the first punishment is as it says in the Midrash (Yelammedenu): "And they traveled" — [meaning] that they traveled from Mount Sinai a distance of three days; like a child leaving school who flees and runs away, so too were they fleeing from Mount Sinai a distance of three days, because they had learned much Torah at Sinai. The Holy One, blessed be He, said: "Shall we juxtapose one punishment to [another] punishment? No! Rather, let us interpose the section of 'And it came to pass when the Ark traveled.'"

Tosafot on Shabbat 116a:7:1.hebrew: ספרי מינין כו', א"ר טרפון כו' - אומר ר"י, דמיירי בנמצאו ביד מינין; דאי כתבן מין — הא אמר בפרק השולח (גיטין דף מה:): "נמצא ביד מין — יגנז, כתבו מין — ישרף", ודוחק לומר דאתי כר"ט ודלא כרבנן ורבי יוסי:
Tosafot on Shabbat 116a:7:1.english: "The scrolls of heretics, etc. Rabbi Tarfon said, etc." - Ri says that [the baraita] is speaking of [scrolls] that were found in the possession of heretics; for if a heretic wrote them — behold, it states in the chapter [entitled] HaSholeach (Gittin 45b): "[If a Torah scroll is] found in the possession of a heretic, it must be buried; [if] a heretic wrote it, it must be burned," and it is forced to say that [that statement in Gittin] follows Rabbi Tarfon and not the Rabbis and Rabbi Yose.

Tosafot on Shabbat 116a:9:1.hebrew: כך אין מצילין אותן לא מן המים כו' - דלא תימא דוקא מן הדליקה אין מצילין, משום דאי שרית ליה אתי לכבויי, אלא אפילו היכא דליכא למיגזר מידי אסור לטלטלן ולהוציאן. והך סיפא כרבנן, דלרבי טרפון לא איצטריך:
Tosafot on Shabbat 116a:9:1.english: So too, they are not rescued, neither from water, etc. - [This is stated] so that you should not say [that] specifically from a fire we do not rescue [them], because if you permit it to him, he might come to extinguish [the fire]; rather, even where there is nothing to decree against, it is forbidden to move them and take them out. And this latter clause is in accordance with the Rabbis, for according to Rabbi Tarfon it is not necessary.
